title: NudgeStreamer.collectNudge credits the buffer with the amount SENT, not received, against a POOLED per-token balance — one taxed token drains sibling streams and bricks batchMint for every reward token
description: `collectNudge` performs `IERC20(token).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount); s.buffer += amount;` (:149-150) with no balance-delta measurement. The streamer holds a SINGLE POOLED balance per token across every `(batchMinter, token)` pair, while `_settle` caps payouts against the per-stream accounting buffer (`_accrued`, :193-200), not against real custody. The contract NatSpec at :194-196 asserts 'The buffer cap guarantees the streamer can never transfer more than it holds, even if elapsed is large' — that guarantee is PER-STREAM whereas custody is POOLED PER-TOKEN, so it does not hold across pairs. The deploy-script probe at DeployMocks.s.sol:1661 is the only defence anywhere and it is VACUOUS: it runs solely against MockKendu and MockPhUSD, both defined with no transfer fee, so it cannot fail locally. There is no on-chain guard.
impact: For any reward token that is fee-on-transfer, taxed, or reflection-based: (1) the credited buffer immediately exceeds custody; (2) whichever `(batchMinter, token)` pair settles first is paid its full over-stated buffer out of the shared balance, consuming the backing of the other pairs; (3) the later pair's `pullPendingStream` REVERTS on insufficient balance; and (4) because `BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.batchMint` loops `pullPendingStream` over `getNudgeTokens()` inside one transaction (:539), a single tainted token bricks batchMint for ALL reward tokens — the entire mint path, not just the tainted reward. Kendu Inu is a memecoin whose real transfer semantics are unverified, and MockKendu's own NatSpec states the mock is deliberately fee-free because the streamer assumes exact delivery.
evidence: PoC workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditDevNudgeStreamerFoT.t.sol — 4/4 PASS against the REAL NudgeStreamer with a 5% fee-on-transfer ERC20. (A) buffer 100,000e18 vs custody 95,000e18. (B) two pairs of the same token: buffers 200,000e18 vs pooled custody 190,000e18; pair A settles and the streamer pays out its full 100,000, leaving 90,000 against pair B's 100,000 claim; B's pullPendingStream reverts. (C) a clean token settles fine in isolation while the tainted token reverts — and batchMint shares one transaction. (D) at feeBps==0 the divergence vanishes entirely, confirming the DeployMocks probe passes vacuously by construction. Also confirmed on the live local chain: streamer balance EXACTLY equals the credited buffer for all three tokens, i.e. the condition under which this finding is invisible.
recommendation: Measure the receipt in `collectNudge`: `uint256 before = IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this)); safeTransferFrom(...); uint256 received = IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this)) - before; s.buffer += received;` and recompute the rate from `received`. If fee-on-transfer tokens are intended to be permanently out of scope, add an on-chain probe in `registerStream` (which is already owner-gated and is the natural admission point) rather than relying on a deploy-script assert against a mock that cannot fail. Independently, verify the real Kendu token's transfer semantics on-chain BEFORE `setNudgeTokenWhitelist` on mainnet.

title: Migration rehearsal sizes the budget transfer as a fraction of a hard-coded CONSTANT rather than of the actual balance — moves 88.67%, not the documented 90%, and strands 345 phUSD in three untracked contracts
propagation: LOCAL-ONLY (but the formula must never be ported — see differential-gap.md §3.1)
description: `uint256 movable = (REHEARSAL_STAKER_BUDGET * 90) / 100;` computes 90% of a hard-coded seed constant, not 90% of the staker's actual phUSD balance. Between the `topUp(REHEARSAL_STAKER_BUDGET)` at :1734 and the migration, the three seed NFT mints route through the Uniboost donation branch and the UniboostMintDebtHook mints additional phUSD INTO the V1 staker. That contribution is excluded from the transfer entirely. The in-source comment at :1822-1830 describes the result as 'a flat 90%' and ':1788' says it 'leaves an arbitrary 10% stranded' — both understate the divergence.
impact: Measured on the live chain: V1 actual balance 1015.014 phUSD, moved 900, so the actual fraction moved is 88.67% and the stranded residual is 115.014 phUSD (11.33%) per staker — 345.042 phUSD across the three. The post-condition at :1712 (`phUSD.balanceOf(v2) > 0`) cannot detect this: it proves non-zero, not correctly-sized. On mainnet, where the mint-debt hook has been minting into the live stakers for months, the seed constant would be an arbitrary and possibly small fraction of the real balance, so 'flat 90%' could move almost any proportion. The author explicitly disclaims the number (:1783-1789: 'Do not read this 90% as a validated answer; the rehearsal proves nothing about sizing') and hands sizing to story 072 as OPEN.
evidence: cast against the deployed chain: three V1 stakers at 0x976fcd02…, 0x413b1afc…, 0x359570b3… hold 115.014007236759570733 / 115.014007236826930907 / 115.014039422670157249 phUSD after migration; the three V2 stakers each hold exactly 900e18 with totalStaked == 3. Staker #3 additionally ended with committedDebt == 1 wei (the others 0), directly confirming the accrual-during-broadcast effect the constant works around is real. None of the six rehearsal artifacts is tracked, so the stranded value is invisible to progress.31337.json, local.json, addresses.ts and the :3001 API.
recommendation: For the mainnet port: compute `balance - committedDebt` at execution time, or move the budget in a separate transaction after `initiateMigration` has frozen `committedDebt`. The forge simulate-then-replay defect that forced the constant does not apply on mainnet, where every `*:broadcast` npm entry uses `--skip-simulation`. Port the ORDERING finding the rehearsal exists to produce (settle+freeze before moving the budget, :1778-1781); do not port the number. Locally, either track the rehearsal artifacts or assert the residual explicitly.

title: BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer is the only one of six streamer setters with no zero-address guard — zeroing it silently strands every accrued stream while batchMint keeps succeeding
description: All six donor contracts reject `setNudgeStreamer(address(0))` with an explicit guard — BalancerPoolerV2.sol:247, Uniboost.sol:191, NudgeRatchet.sol:106, PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol:349, StableYieldAccumulator.sol:514. `BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer` (:299-302) has none, because address(0) is its deliberate 'streaming disabled' sentinel: `batchMint` gates the whole `pullPendingStream` loop on `if (_nudgeStreamer != address(0))` (:538). The sentinel design is defensible in isolation; the hazard is that it is the ONE setter in a family of six that accepts the value every sibling rejects, and its failure mode is silent while every sibling's is a loud revert.
impact: An operator wiring the sink from a wrong or placeholder address (see DEV-06) gets no error and no event distinguishable from a normal reconfiguration. batchMint continues to succeed. Every accrued stream stays stranded in the streamer and the batcher is paid only whatever was already sitting in the sink. Because `pullPendingStream` is the ONLY path by which streamed funds reach the batch minter, and donors keep pushing INTO the streamer, the divergence grows without bound and is visible only by comparing streamer buffers against sink balances. This inverts the intuition an operator would form from the five guarded siblings.
evidence: PoC workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditDevStreamerWiring.t.sol, run with --fork-url against the live local chain — 2/2 PASS. test_zeroAddressGuardAsymmetry: all six donors return ok==false for setNudgeStreamer(address(0)); BatchNFTMinterMultiToken returns ok==true and nudgeStreamer() reads address(0). test_zeroedSinkStrandsAccruedStreams: with the streamer wired, a qualifying batchMint(26) pays the batcher 45,045,015 USDC + 5,000e18 phUSD + 50,000e18 Kendu; with the streamer zeroed the SAME batchMint SUCCEEDS with no revert and no event and pays 189,464 USDC + 0 phUSD + 0 Kendu, leaving the full matured pot stranded in the streamer.
recommendation: Either (a) emit a distinct, unambiguous event when the streamer is set to zero (e.g. `NudgeStreamingDisabled`) so the disable is loud in logs, or (b) add an explicit `setNudgeStreamingEnabled(bool)` and require a non-zero address in `setNudgeStreamer`, separating 'disable' from 'misconfigure'. At minimum, the mainnet script must post-assert `batchMinter.nudgeStreamer() == <expected>` after the call — DeployMocks post-asserts only the SYA leg (:1129) of seven such calls.

title: progress.31337.json is written with a hard-coded deploymentStatus "completed" during forge's local-execution phase, before any transaction is broadcast
propagation: PROPAGATES-TO-MAINNET (as a pattern — this shape has already poisoned three committed mainnet progress files)
description: `_writeProgressFile()` emits `"deploymentStatus": "completed"` as a string LITERAL (:1922), derived from nothing, and is called after `vm.stopBroadcast()` — i.e. during forge's local execution pass, before the broadcast begins. The file also hard-codes `"chainId": 31337` (:1919) rather than reading `block.chainid`, and hard-codes its own output path (:1943). It contains no timestamp and no deployer field, so a stale file is byte-indistinguishable from a fresh one.
impact: Benign in isolation on anvil — DeployMocks never reads a progress file (no vm.readFile/parseJson anywhere) and clean:local deletes it first, so there is no resume consumer to mislead. It is NOT benign as a pattern: package.json's `//uniboost-cutover:resume` doc comment records this exact shape already producing three committed `progress.uniboost-cutover.1.POISONED*.bak` files on mainnet, where a crashed broadcast left a file positively asserting completion. Combined with the total absence of a chain-id guard (DEV-05), a mis-pointed RPC would produce a progress file that positively asserts it is anvil output.
evidence: Empirically confirmed during this audit: progress.31337.json mtime 2026-07-29 12:14:24 while the broadcast was still in flight at 12:17:45 (deployer nonce 160 of 352). The file claimed 'completed' for a further ~15 minutes of unconfirmed broadcasting. Separately, a cold redeploy reproduced the committed file BYTE-IDENTICALLY (md5 f4bb1d9f42d24416dd8a4622ab6b21c7), which is a positive determinism result but also means no field distinguishes a fresh file from a stale one.
recommendation: For the mainnet port, do not inherit this. Use `DeployMainnetUniboostBatchMinters.s.sol:214`'s `_isDeployed` (which additionally requires `a.code.length > 0`) as the source of truth for resume, and treat the progress file as advisory. Locally, at minimum read `block.chainid` rather than hard-coding 31337, and add a timestamp so staleness is detectable.

title: DeployMocks has no block.chainid guard at all, in direct contravention of the project's own CLAUDE.md, while every DeployMainnet* script carries one twice
propagation: LOCAL-ONLY (the guard's absence is the finding; the port must add one)
description: Line :290 merely LOGS the chain id. There is no `require(block.chainid == 31337)` anywhere in the 1946-line file. All seven DeployMainnet* scripts carry `require(block.chainid == 1)`, most of them twice (setUp + run). The project's own CLAUDE.md is explicit: 'Anvil may relax these checks for local iteration, but the relaxation must be gated behind an explicit `block.chainid == 31337` branch and clearly commented — never share an unsafe default code path between local and real networks.' The same file also lists 'Mock contracts with unlimited minting / Default Anvil private keys / Unrestricted permissions / Simplified initialization' under 'Local Development Only — NEVER deploy these configurations to Sepolia or Mainnet.'
impact: Story 073 enlarges the ungated surface: unrestricted `MockKendu.mint`, `phUSD.setMinter(deployer, true)` granted at :1648 and :1731 and never revoked (verified live: `authorizedMinters(deployer) == (true, 1)` after the run), the 300-ETH `WETH9.deposit` at :1460, real `PhusdStableMinter.mint` calls in Phases 9/9.5/9.55/9.6, and the entire destructive V1-staker teardown (pause + pauser repoint to an EOA + unregister from the global Pauser). The only thing preventing this script from running against a non-anvil RPC is the operator typing the right --rpc-url. This is a footgun in the Law-3 sense: a competent non-malicious operator would be surprised that the one script in the repo containing every unsafe local relaxation is also the only one with no chain gate.
evidence: grep for `block.chainid` in script/DeployMocks.s.sol returns a single hit at :290, inside a console.log. grep for `setMinter(.*false)` returns nothing. Live post-run: `cast call MockPhUSD 'authorizedMinters(address)' 0xf39Fd6e5… -> (true, 1)`, `mintVersion() -> 1`.
recommendation: Add `require(block.chainid == 31337, "DeployMocks: anvil only")` in `run()` before `vm.startBroadcast`. Independently, revoke the two `phUSD.setMinter(deployer, true)` grants at the end of the run and post-assert `authorizedMinters(deployer).canMint == false`, so the port inherits a revoke-and-assert habit rather than a standing grant.

title: mainnet-addresses.ts carries 0x0 placeholders for Kendu and NudgeStreamer that are type-indistinguishable from real addresses, because the ContractAddresses interface is regenerated from ANVIL data with every field a required plain string
description: `generate-ts-addresses.js` regenerates `addresses.ts`'s `ContractAddresses` interface from local.json — i.e. from ANVIL data — emitting `${name}: string;` for every one of the 57 keys, all required, all plain `string`. The hand-maintained `mainnet-addresses.ts` is annotated `: ContractAddresses`, so a purely local mock addition forces a placeholder into the mainnet address book. Story-073 commit d241e61 did exactly that for `Kendu` (:64) and `NudgeStreamer` (:131), both `0x0000…0000`. Nothing in the type system, the file, or the :3001 API distinguishes a placeholder from a real address.
impact: A mainnet script sourcing `NudgeStreamer` or `Kendu` from this file gets address(0). IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the prior framing: this does NOT produce a silent mis-wire on the donor path — all six donors reject `setNudgeStreamer(address(0))` explicitly, and `setNudgeTokenWhitelist(address(0), true)` reverts `BatchMint__ZeroNudgeToken`, so those legs fail LOUDLY at deploy time. The one silent consumer is `BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer`, which has no guard (see DEV-03). The residual risk is therefore (a) that one silent leg and (b) a general operator-trust problem: the file's zero addresses read as data, not as 'not yet deployed'.
evidence: server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts:64 `Kendu: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"`, :131 `NudgeStreamer: "0x00…00"`. server/generate-ts-addresses.js:57 `lines.push(\`  ${name}: string;\`)`. Live run: addresses.ts regenerated with 57 required string fields; the :3001 API serves both `Kendu` and `NudgeStreamer` with no mock/placeholder marker and zero `Mock`-prefixed keys.
recommendation: Introduce a branded or optional type for not-yet-deployed entries (e.g. `NudgeStreamer?: string` or a `type NotDeployed = "0x0"` union) so the compiler distinguishes them, or split the interface into a mainnet-required core and an anvil-only extension so local mock additions stop type-gating the mainnet address book. At minimum, add a runtime guard in any mainnet script: `require(addr != address(0), "<name> not deployed")` at the point of read.

title: mainnet-addresses.ts comments describe three REAL non-zero mainnet addresses as "not yet deployed / zero placeholders", inverting exactly the distinction the mainnet port depends on
description: The comments at :136 and :142 read 'NudgeRatchet dispatcher + its mint-debt hook — not yet deployed on mainnet (story 068). Zero placeholders so this file still satisfies the ContractAddresses interface' and 'Dedicated NFTStaker … not yet deployed on mainnet (story 068)'. The values beneath them are real, non-zero, deployed mainnet addresses: NudgeRatchet 0xd4ea91f6096A75a1c34A3c25D7725dE1f5c49f68, NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook 0x09AceB96337df1316e0D2d7EEEa44d754D1f8d05, RatchetNFTStaker 0x299b0071def42d35eaf5ea24cc0a71cf10655a64, RatchetBatchNFTMinter 0x81896f48a95abea255cd38a3010e985b6051a1c7.
impact: Seventy lines above, two entries in the SAME file genuinely are zero placeholders (DEV-06). An operator reading this file to decide what still needs deploying gets the answer exactly backwards for four entries. Given the stated next step is a hand-written differential mainnet script that must source live addresses from this file and distinguish deployed from not-deployed, this is the single most decision-relevant piece of misinformation in the address book. It is also a Law-3 footgun: the comment is the artifact a competent operator would trust.
evidence: Direct read of server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts:136-145. Corroborated by package.json's `//fix-ratchet-sink` doc comment, which describes live owner-only operations against the NudgeRatchet and RatchetBatchNFTMinter — i.e. contracts that are demonstrably deployed and in production use.
recommendation: Correct the four comments to record the actual deployment dates and the story that shipped them. Adopt a single, machine-checkable convention for 'not yet deployed' (see DEV-06) so a comment can never contradict a value. Consider a lint/CI check asserting that any entry commented 'not yet deployed' holds address(0) and vice versa.

title: extract-addresses.js strips a leading "Mock" before every drop-list and rename, and writes the result with no collision guard
propagation: PROPAGATES-TO-MAINNET (the interface it generates gates the mainnet address book)
description: `const displayName = name.startsWith('Mock') ? name.slice(4) : name;` (:107) is a blind 4-character slice applied BEFORE the DROPPED_CONTRACT_NAMES check (:110), the UniV2-backing drop (:116), the V1-NFT drop (:122) and the V2->base rename (:137-141). The final write at :144 is an unguarded assignment with no duplicate detection. Separately, three mocks bypass the strip entirely because they are tracked under an already-stripped key (MockUSDe as 'USDe' :327, MockSUSDe as 'SUSDe' :333, MockMarketAMMAdapter as 'USDeAMMAdapter' :446), so the file carries two conventions for the same job.
impact: Two effects. (1) Nothing downstream marks a mock as a mock — verified on the live run: local.json, addresses.ts, local-addresses.ts and the :3001 API contain ZERO keys beginning with 'Mock'; MockPhUSD is served as 'PhUSD', MockKendu as 'Kendu', MockAutoDOLA as 'AutoDOLA'. A UI or operator reading the address book cannot tell a 22-line stub from the real Balancer router. (2) The missing collision guard is a latent silent-clobber: a future contract tracked as 'MockNFTMinterV2' would strip to NFTMinterV2, hit the V2 rename, and overwrite the REAL 'NFTMinter' key with no error; one tracked as 'MockNFTMigrator' would be silently dropped. No collision exists today (verified across all 99 track keys), but the mainnet key set is hand-maintained and must mirror this generated interface exactly, so a silent overwrite points the UI at the wrong contract.
evidence: server/extract-addresses.js:107, :144. Live run: 71 progress entries -> 57 local.json entries; `curl localhost:3001/contracts` returns 57 keys, 0 of which start with 'Mock', including 'Kendu' and 'NudgeStreamer'.
recommendation: Add a duplicate-key assertion before the write at :144 (`if (extracted.contracts[displayName]) throw new Error(...)`). Move the Mock strip AFTER the drop-lists and rename so it cannot interact with them. Consider emitting an `isMock: true` flag on stripped entries so the UI and the :3001 API can surface the distinction rather than erasing it.

title: DeployMocks asserts none of story 073's headline stream state, and the one probe that covers it is vacuous by construction
description: The script's 17 requires include no post-condition on `streams(batchMinter, token).duration == LOCAL_STREAM_DURATION`, on any buffer being non-zero, or on `pendingStream` accruing — the three facts story 073 exists to establish. Of the seven `setNudgeStreamer` calls only the SYA leg is post-asserted (:1129). The one probe touching stream state (:1661/:1664) runs solely against MockKendu and MockPhUSD, both fee-free by construction, so it cannot fail (see DEV-01).
impact: The story's reported outcome rests on console.log output rather than on-chain assertions, so a regression in the wiring would produce a green run. NOTE IN MITIGATION: the author's technical reason for not asserting accrual in-script is sound and documented at script/interactions/TestNudgePayout.s.sol:157-168 — a forge script's requires all execute in the simulation pass where every statement shares one block timestamp, so `pendingStream` reads 0 there regardless of the live chain. This is a genuine tooling constraint, not negligence. The gap is therefore in the RUNBOOK, not the script: nothing in the `dev` chain performs the out-of-band verification the author says is required.
evidence: This audit performed the missing verification with cast and confirmed all three self-reported numbers: duration == 21600 on all three tokens; buffers USDC 44855551 (44.855551, matching the reported '44.86'), phUSD 5000e18, Kendu 50000e18; pendingStream non-zero on all three; streamer ERC20 balance exactly equal to each credited buffer.
recommendation: Add the out-of-band verification to the `dev` chain as a scripted step (a `verify:streams` npm entry doing the cast reads and failing non-zero), so the property is enforced rather than documented. Post-assert all seven `setNudgeStreamer` calls, not just SYA. The same verification step is required in the mainnet runbook — see differential-gap.md §4.5.

title: MockERC4626Wrapper is deployed, pre-funded with 1,000,000 mock USDC and exported to the UI as WaUSDC, but serves a route removed in story-034 and has zero first-party consumers
description: The sUSDS->waUSDC donation route this mock serves was replaced by the Sky PSM in story-034 and is described in-source as 'structurally dead' (BalancerPoolerV2.sol:23-29). Its only caller is MockBalancerVault.swap (:165), which is itself never invoked by first-party code (zero `swap(` hits in BalancerPoolerV2.sol). The mock is nevertheless deployed at DeployMocks.s.sol:677, funded with 1,000,000 mock USDC at :686, and exported to the address book and the :3001 API as `WaUSDC`.
impact: Noise in the address book that the UI and any operator reading it must ignore. The mock's `mintShares` is unauthenticated and its `redeem` enforces no allowance (:54-56, :64-68), so the 1M is freely drainable by anyone on the local chain — harmless on anvil, but it means a contract with no purpose holds the largest single mock balance in the deployment. MockBalancerVault.swap/setSwapRate are dead for the same reason.
evidence: grep for `swap(` in lib/yield-claim-nft/src/dispatchers/BalancerPoolerV2.sol returns zero hits. MockERC4626Wrapper appears in local.json and in `curl localhost:3001/contracts` as `WaUSDC`.
recommendation: Delete MockERC4626Wrapper, its deployment and funding steps, and MockBalancerVault.swap/setSwapRate. Do not carry any of it into the mainnet port.

title: The :3001 API's root doc blob advertises 18 available contracts while the endpoint serves 57, and CORS is open to every origin
description: `GET /` returns a static documentation blob listing a hand-written `availableContracts` array of 18 names; `GET /contracts` actually serves 57. Both loaders are hard-wired to chainId 31337 and the response shape does not match the `{networks:{...}, activeNetwork, availableNetworks}` contract documented in the project CLAUDE.md. `cors()` is applied with no origin allowlist.
impact: A UI developer integrating against the documented surface sees a third of what exists. Local-only and low consequence — anvil binds loopback here, though `npm run start:anvil` uses `--host 0.0.0.0`, which binds every interface.
evidence: Live run: `curl localhost:3001/` -> availableContracts length 18; `curl localhost:3001/contracts` -> 57 keys. Health endpoint confirms deploymentsLoaded/extractedAddressesLoaded true, chainId 31337.
recommendation: Derive the root blob's contract list from local.json rather than hand-maintaining it, or drop the list and point at /contracts. Reconcile the response shape with CLAUDE.md, or update CLAUDE.md to describe what is actually served.
